summary: Hans Kamstrup Vogt worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the universities of Oslo, Paris, and Yale, and under Antoine Meillet and Edward Sapir. He served as Professor of General Linguistics at Oslo from 1946 to 1973.
Hans Karl Siegert was a linguist. He studied at the University of Munich from circa 1935 to 1939 under Walther Wüst.

Linguist Hans Krahe earned his Ph.D. at the University of Jena under Friedrich Karl Slotty and studied under Ferdinand Sommer. He held academic posts at Jena, the University of Würzburg, Heidelberg University, and the University of Tübingen.

Hans Küng was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum, and Institut Catholique de Paris, and served at the University of Tübingen from circa 1960 to 1996.

Hans Losch was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich and the University of Bonn, learning under Hermann Jacobi and Willibald Kirfel. He spent his career at the University of Bonn as Privatdozent, professor, and wissenschaftlicher Rat.

Hans Much worked in Buddhist studies and medicine. He studied at the universities of Marburg, Kiel, and Berlin, earned his Dr.med. at the University of Würzburg, and became Professor of Medicine at the University of Hamburg in 1919.

Hans Nordewin von Körber was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics who studied at Berlin, Bonn, Cambridge, and Marburg. From circa 1928 to 1962, he was Professor of Oriental Studies at the University of Southern California.

Hans Reichelt studied Indology, linguistics, and Iranian studies at Vienna and Giessen under Bühler, Meringer, Müller, and Bartholomae. He held positions at Innsbruck, Chernivtsi, Graz (where he served as Rector in 1920), and the University of Hamburg.

Hans Schacht specialized in Indology and linguistics, completing his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin. He taught at École Normale Cantonale de Lausanne and Gymnase de la Cité, and served as Privatdozent of Sanskrit at the University of Lausanne.

Indologist and religious studies scholar Hans T. Bakker studied under Jacob Ensink. He held posts at Utrecht University and the University of Groningen, served as a curator at the British Museum, and held visiting positions at Oxford, Vienna, and Kyoto.
Hans Urs von Balthasar worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Zurich from circa 1923 to 1928 and studied under Bernhard Geiger from 1924 to 1926.
Hans West was an Indologist who studied at Odense Katedralskole. In 1788, he served as rector at the Danish School in Christiansted.

Hans Wilhelm Haussig studied Iranian and Central Asian studies and history, completing his Ph.D. at Berlin under Robert Bleichsteiner. He later taught at the Free University of Berlin and served as professor at Ruhr University Bochum from 1969 to 1982.
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1926–1929), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1929–1935).

Hans Wirtz worked in Indology and Sinology. He studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Bonn, completing a doctorate under Hermann Jacobi, and later served as a teacher at the University of Cologne from 1922 to 1929.

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit was a scholar of religion, Iranian and Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and Gustav Mensching at Tübingen and Bonn, also attending Harvard, and later served as a director at Bonn.
Hans-Joachim Rassat was an Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Tübingen, where he studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp from circa 1948 to 1955.

Hans-Rudolf Kantor specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Educated at Delhi, National Taiwan University, and Bonn, he has held academic posts at Huafan University, Tamkang University, Fo Guang Shan, Fo Guang University, and National Chengchi University.
Hans-Ulrich Rieker was active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied as a disciple under Anagarika Govinda, founded Arya Maitreya Mandala in 1952, and served as its leader until circa 1964.
Hans-Werbin Köhler was an Indologist. He studied under Eduard Hermann and completed his doctoral work under Ernst Waldschmidt by 1948.
